Glyphosate herbicide negatively affects key soil organisms, belowground interactions between earthworms and symbiotic mycorrhizal fungi in a model ecosystem
Poor mycelium. It is the source of life and it's decay is the death of soil.
And it allows trees and other plants to shuttle nutrients in the soil web. Fungi is incredibly important and fascinating.
The same is true of most pesticides afaik. Not a surprise really.

It's really a shame, but very obvious when you understand how soil organisms work. First and foremost they need to eat. Some prey on eachother, but fungi are the only real "producers" in the soil. This means a lot of the organisms feed off plant roots (while living). They release exudates that really make up the bottom of the pyramid In the rhizosphere. Everything else follows. When a plant dies naturally or sheds its leaves for the season, a herd of hungry microbes come and clean up the debris and enrich the soil even further.

When you constantly spray the same patch or earth there are no plant to feed the microbes or shade the soil from the harsh sun. Then all live ceases to exist and you end up with sterile inert soil. If we change our focus from thinking soil is just a combination of nutrients, to understanding it is a diverse ecosystem. And those microbe's waste is what actually feed plants, we just might un-fuck the agriculture industry. Basically, permaculture.
